record.original_question: Let p be the number of distinct processing times. Are each of the three preemptive parallel-machine problems P|pmtn,r_j|sum C_j, P|pmtn|sum U_j, and P|pmtn|sum T_j fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by p?

evidence.quote: The three problems P|pmtn,rj|ΣCj, P|pmtn|ΣUj, and P|pmtn|ΣT j are all NP-hard.
Open Problem 9. Are the above problems fixed-parameter tractable parameterized by the number p of distinct processing times?
Preemption. Per default, we assume that jobs are not allowed to be preempted. Otherwise, we add “pmtn” to the β-field.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider scheduling on m identical parallel machines. An instance consists of n jobs, where each job j has a positive integer processing time p_j and (in problems with release dates) a non-negative integer release date r_j; depending on the problem, each job may also have a due date d_j. Preemption is allowed: at any moment a job currently being processed on some machine may be interrupted and later resumed (possibly on a different machine), with the constraint that no job is processed on two machines simultaneously and no machine processes two jobs simultaneously. The completion time of job j in a schedule is denoted C_j. For due-date variants, U_j = 1 if C_j > d_j and 0 otherwise (the job is "late"), and T_j = max(0, C_j − d_j) is the tardiness of job j.

Let p denote the number of distinct values among the processing times p_1, …, p_n.

Decide, for each of the following three problems, whether it is fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by p, i.e., whether there exists an algorithm solving the problem in time f(p) · |I|^{O(1)} for some computable function f, where |I| is the input size:

(i) P | pmtn, r_j | ∑ C_j: minimize the sum of completion times with release dates and preemption on identical parallel machines.

(ii) P | pmtn | ∑ U_j: minimize the number of late jobs with preemption on identical parallel machines.

(iii) P | pmtn | ∑ T_j: minimize total tardiness with preemption on identical parallel machines.

All three problems are known to be NP-hard.
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not surface a published resolution establishing fixed-parameter tractability (or W[1]-hardness) of these three preemptive parallel-machine scheduling problems parameterized by the number of distinct processing times. The question was posed as an open problem in a survey of parameterized scheduling complexity, and no follow-up source clearly settling all three cases was found.

status_evidence.claim: The problem is listed as open in the survey of open parameterized scheduling problems.

status_evidence.title: Scheduling Meets Fixed-Parameter Tractability
status_evidence.snippet: Parameterizing by the number of distinct processing times yields FPT algorithms for several scheduling problems via convex integer programming.
status_evidence.claim: FPT results by number of distinct processing times exist for related but different scheduling problems; no result covering the three preemptive cases here was found.
